title: The gospel commands as divine teaching leading to heaven
english: The gospel precepts, dearly beloved brothers, are nothing other than divine teachings: foundations of hope to be built, supports of faith to be strengthened, nourishment of the heart to be cherished, rudders of the journey to be directed, protections of salvation to be obtained. While they instruct the teachable minds of believers on earth, they lead them through to the heavenly kingdom. God willed that many things be said and heard through the prophets his servants, but how much greater are the things the Son speaks, which the Word of God who was in the prophets testifies with his own voice—no longer commanding that a way be prepared for one who is coming, but himself coming and opening the way for us and showing it, so that we who previously wandered improvident and blind in the darkness of death, having been enlightened by the light of grace, might hold to the path of life with the Lord as guide and director.
orientation: Cyprian opens the treatise by addressing his fellow Christians and describing the gospel commands as God's teaching that guides believers from earth to heaven.

title: Christ gave the form of prayer
english: Among the rest of his saving warnings and divine precepts by which he provides for his people's salvation, he also gave us the form of praying himself; he himself taught and instructed us what we should pray for. He who made us live also taught us to pray, with that same kindness by which he deigned to give and bestow all other things, so that when we speak to the Father in the prayer and petition the Son taught, we may be heard more easily. He had already foretold that the hour was coming when true worshippers would worship the Father in spirit and truth, and he fulfilled what he promised before, so that we who have received spirit and truth from his sanctification may also worship truly and spiritually according to his teaching. For what prayer can be spiritual except the one given to us by Christ, from whom the Holy Spirit was also sent to us? What true petition before the Father can there be except the one brought forth from the mouth of the Son, who is truth? So to pray otherwise than he taught is not only ignorance but also fault, since he himself declared and said: “You reject the commandment of God, to establish your own tradition” (Mark 7:9).
orientation: Cyprian is explaining that Christ, among his saving commands, himself gave the form and words of prayer so that Christians may be heard by the Father.

title: Praying with Christ's own words
english: So let us pray, most beloved brothers, as God our teacher taught us. It is a friendly and familiar prayer to ask God with his own words, to send up Christ's prayer to his ears. Let the Father recognize his Son's words when we make our prayer. Let him who dwells inside in the breast be also in the voice, and since we have him as advocate with the Father for our sins, when we sinners plead for forgiveness of our offenses, let us bring forth the words of our advocate. For since he says that whatever we ask the Father in his name he will give us (John 16:23), how much more effectively do we obtain what we ask in Christ's name, if we ask with his own prayer?
orientation: Cyprian is addressing his fellow Christians, urging them to pray as Christ taught, because the Lord's Prayer is the Son's own prayer to the Father.

title: Prayer must be quiet, modest, and mindful of God's presence
english: But when we pray, our speech and prayer should be disciplined, quiet, and modest. Let us remember that we are standing under the sight of God. We must please the divine eyes both by the posture of our body and by the tone of our voice. For just as it is the mark of a shameless person to make a din with shoutings, so it is fitting for a modest person to pray with restrained prayers. Finally, the Lord by his own teaching commanded us to pray in secret, in hidden and secluded places, in our very bedchambers. This is more in keeping with faith, so that we may know that God is present everywhere, that he hears and sees all things, and that in the fullness of his majesty he penetrates even hidden and secret places. As it is written: "I am a God who draws near, and not a God far off. If a person hides himself in secret places, will I not see him? Do I not fill heaven and earth?" (Jeremiah 23:23-24). And again: "In every place the eyes of God watch the good and the evil" (Proverbs 15:3). And when we gather together with the brothers and celebrate the divine sacrifices with God's priest, we ought to remember modesty and discipline. We should not scatter our prayers here and there with unformed voices, nor throw about with noisy talkativeness a petition that should be commended to God with restraint. For God is the hearer not of the voice but of the heart. He does not need to be prompted by shoutings, since he sees our thoughts, as the Lord proves when he says: "Why do you think evil in your hearts?" (Matthew 9:4). And in another place: "And all the churches will know that I am the one who searches minds and hearts" (Revelation 2:23).
orientation: Cyprian is teaching how Christians should pray, now turning from the Lord's Prayer itself to the manner and disposition of prayer.

title: Anna's silent prayer as the church's model
english: Anna, who bears the type of the church in the first book of 1 Samuel, kept and preserved this. She was not praying to God with a clamorous petition, but silently and modestly within the very hiding places of her breast. She was speaking with hidden prayer but with manifest faith. She was speaking not with her voice but with her heart, because she knew that this is how the Lord hears. And she obtained effectively what she asked, because she asked faithfully. The divine Scripture declares this when it says: “She was speaking in her heart, and her lips were moving, and her voice was not heard, and the Lord heard her” (1 Samuel 1:13). We also read in the Psalms: “Speak in your hearts, and be pricked on your beds” (Psalm 4:4). Through Jeremiah also the Holy Spirit suggests and teaches these same things, saying: “But in the mind you ought to be worshipped, O Lord.”
orientation: Cyprian is beginning his treatise by showing from Scripture that prayer is heard when it is humble and inward, and he now presents Anna in 1 Samuel as a type of the church.

title: The publican's humble prayer heard over the Pharisee's pride
english: But when he worships, dearest brothers, let him not be ignorant of how the publican prayed in the temple with the Pharisee. He did not lift his eyes shamelessly to heaven or raise his hands insolently. He was striking his breast and bearing witness to the sins shut up within, and he was imploring the help of divine mercy. And while the Pharisee was pleasing to himself, this man who prayed in this way deserved more to be made holy, because he did not place his hope of salvation in confidence in his own innocence—since no one is innocent—but confessed his sins and prayed humbly. And the one who forgives the humble heard him as he prayed. The Lord sets this down in his Gospel and says: “Two men went up to the temple to worship, one a Pharisee and one a publican. The Pharisee stood and was praying these things to himself: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like other men—unjust, robbers, adulterers—or even like this publican. I fast twice in the week; I give tithes of everything I possess.’ But the publican stood far off and would not even lift his eyes to heaven, but was striking his breast, saying: ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner.’ I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than that Pharisee. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted” (Luke 18:10-14).
orientation: Cyprian is addressing his beloved brothers, teaching from the Gospel how one ought to pray by contrasting the Pharisee and the publican in the temple.

title: Learning what to pray from the Lord's teaching
english: Now that we have learned from the divine reading how we ought to approach prayer, most beloved brothers, let us learn with the Lord teaching us what we should pray. “Thus,” he says, “pray: Our Father, who are in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors. And do not allow us to be led into temptation, but deliver us from evil” (Matthew 6:9-13).
orientation: Cyprian is addressing his fellow Christians, having just shown from the parable of the Pharisee and the publican how one should approach prayer, and now turns to the Lord's own words teaching what to pray.

title: Public and common prayer
english: Above all, the teacher of peace and master of unity did not want prayer to be made one by one and privately, so that when someone prays he prays only for himself. We do not say, “My Father, who are in heaven,” nor “Give me my bread today.” No one asks that his debt be forgiven for himself alone, or begs for himself alone not to be led into temptation and to be delivered from evil. The prayer is public and common for us, and when we pray, we pray not for one person but for the whole people, because the whole people are one. God, the teacher of peace and concord who taught unity, wanted one to pray for all in this way, just as he himself carried all in the one. The three children shut inside the fiery furnace kept this law of prayer, harmonious in their petition and united in the agreement of the Spirit. The witness of divine Scripture makes this clear, and while it teaches how they prayed, it gives us an example to imitate in our prayers, so that we may be able to be like them. “Then,” it says, “those three were singing a hymn as if from one mouth and blessing God” (Daniel 3:51). They spoke as if from one mouth, and Christ had not yet taught them to pray. And so their speech earned the Lord's favor and was effective for them as they prayed, because a peaceful, simple, and spiritual prayer deserved the Lord's response. In the same way we find that the apostles prayed with the disciples after the Lord’s ascension. “They were all persevering with one mind in prayer,” it says, “with the women and Mary, who had been the mother of Jesus, and his brothers” (Acts 1:14). They were persevering in prayer with one mind, showing by their urgency and their unity together that God, who makes those of one mind dwell in a house, does not admit anyone into the divine and eternal house except where there is unanimous prayer.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining why the Lord's Prayer uses 'our' rather than 'my,' grounding this in the unity of the whole people of God.

title: The new birth teaches us to call God Father
english: What mysteries the Lord's Prayer contains, dearly beloved brothers—how many, how great! They are gathered briefly in words, yet spiritually rich in power, so that nothing at all is left out that is not included in this summary of heavenly teaching for our prayers and petitions. "Pray like this," he says: "Our Father, who are in heaven" (Matthew 6:9). The new man, reborn and restored to his God through his grace, says "Father" first of all, because he has now begun to be a son. "He came to his own," he says, "and his own did not receive him. But to all who received him he gave power to become children of God, to those who believe in his name" (John 1:11-12). So whoever has believed in his name and become a child of God must begin from this point: he must give thanks and confess that he is God's child, and when he names God as his Father in heaven, he must also bear witness in the very first words of his new birth that he has renounced the earthly and fleshly father and has begun to know and have only the Father who is in heaven. As it is written: "They who say to their father and mother, 'I do not know you,' and do not acknowledge their own children—these have kept your precepts and preserved your covenant" (Deuteronomy 33:9). Likewise the Lord commanded in his gospel that we should call no one on earth our father, because there is one Father for us, who is in heaven (Matthew 23:9). And to the disciple who mentioned his dead father, he answered: "Let the dead bury their own dead" (Matthew 8:22). For the disciple had said his father was dead, but the Father of believers is living.
orientation: Cyprian has just begun his treatise and now opens his explanation of the Lord's Prayer by showing that the address 'our Father' belongs only to those reborn as God's children.

title: Only the reborn may call God Father
english: Nor should we only notice and understand this, dearly beloved brothers, that we call upon the Father who is in heaven. We also join ourselves together and say “our Father”—that is, the Father of those who believe, of those who have been sanctified through him and restored by the spiritual birth of grace, and so have begun to be children of God. This word also strikes and smites the Jews, because they not only faithlessly rejected Christ, who had been announced to them through the prophets and sent to them first, but cruelly killed him. They can no longer call the Lord “Father,” since the Lord confounds and rebukes them, saying: “You were born of your father the devil, and you want to carry out your father’s desires. He was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him” (John 8:44). And through the prophet Isaiah God cries out in indignation: “I have begotten children and raised them up, but they have rejected me. The ox knows its owner and the donkey its master’s manger, but Israel has not known me, and my people has not understood. Woe to a sinful nation, a people full of sins, wicked seed, criminal children. You have forsaken the Lord and have provoked to indignation the Holy One of Israel” (Isaiah 1:2-4). To their reproach, when we Christians pray we say “our Father,” because he has now begun to be ours and has ceased to be the Father of the Jews who abandoned him. Nor can a sinful people be children; rather, to those to whom forgiveness of sins is given, the name of children is assigned, and to them eternity is promised, as the Lord himself says: “Everyone who commits sin is a slave. A slave does not remain in the house forever; a son remains forever” (John 8:34-35).
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the opening words of the Lord's Prayer, now focusing on the word 'our' and its exclusion of the Jews who rejected Christ.

title: Living as children of the Father we name
english: How great is the Lord’s kindness, how great his condescension toward us and the abundance of his goodness! He willed us to perform prayer in God’s presence in this way. We call the Lord Father. As Christ is the Son of God, so we are named children of God. None of us would dare to take up that name in prayer, unless he himself had given us leave to pray like this.

So, dearest brothers, we must remember and know this. When we call God Father, we must act as children of God. As we delight in God as Father, so he must delight in us. Let us live as temples of God, so that it is plain the Lord dwells in us. Let no act of ours fall away from the Spirit. We have begun to be spiritual and heavenly, so let us think and do only what is spiritual and heavenly. For the Lord God himself has said: “Those who glorify me I will glorify, and those who despise me shall be despised” (1 Samuel 2:30). And the blessed apostle Paul has also set it down in his letter: “You are not your own, for you were bought at a great price. Glorify God and bear him in your body” (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).
orientation: Cyprian has explained calling God our Father and now draws out what that name requires of the reborn.

title: Hallowed be your name: daily sanctification
english: After this we say: hallowed be your name. We do not mean that we wish God to be hallowed by our prayers, but that we ask the Lord that his name may be hallowed in us. Besides, by whom is God hallowed, since he himself hallows? But because he himself said: "Be holy, for I too am holy" (Leviticus 11:44), we ask and beg this: that we who were hallowed in baptism may persevere in what we have begun to be. And we pray for this daily. For we need a daily hallowing, so that we who sin daily may cleanse our sins by constant hallowing. What this hallowing is that is conferred on us by God's gracious favor, the apostle proclaims when he says: "Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor soft men, nor pursuers of males, nor thieves, nor swindlers, nor drunkards, nor the abusive, nor robbers will obtain the kingdom of God. And such were some of you. But you were washed, but you were justified, but you were hallowed in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God" (1 Corinthians 6:9-11). He says that we are hallowed in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God. We pray that this hallowing may remain in us, and because our Lord and judge warns the man he has healed and made alive not to sin any more, so that nothing worse happens to him, we make this prayer with unceasing petitions. Day and night we ask this: that the hallowing and making alive that is received from God's grace may be preserved by his protection.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the first petition of the Lord's Prayer, 'hallowed be your name,' after having discussed the opening address 'our Father.'

title: The coming of the kingdom of God
english: The prayer continues: your kingdom come. We ask that the kingdom of God also be brought near to us, just as we ask that his name be hallowed in us. For when does God not reign, or when does that begin with him which always was and never ceases to be? We ask that our kingdom come, the kingdom promised to us by God, won by the blood and passion of Christ, so that we who before served in the world may afterwards reign with Christ ruling, as he himself promises and says: come, blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the origin of the world (Matthew 25:34). But truly, most beloved brothers, Christ himself can also be the kingdom of God, whom we desire to come daily, whose coming we long to have brought near to us quickly. For since he himself is the resurrection, because in him we rise again, so also he himself can be understood as the kingdom of God, because in him we are going to reign. And we do well to ask for the kingdom of God, that is, the heavenly kingdom, because there is also an earthly kingdom. But he who has already renounced the world is greater than its honors and its kingdom. And therefore he who dedicates himself to God and Christ desires not earthly but heavenly kingdoms. But we need constant prayer and petition, lest we fall away from the heavenly kingdom, just as the Jews, to whom this was first promised, fell away, as the Lord shows and proves. Many, he says, will come from east and west and will recline with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven. But the children of the kingdom will be cast out into outer darkness: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth (Matthew 8:11-12). He shows that the Jews were formerly children of the kingdom, when they also continued to be children of God. After the fatherly name ceased among them, the kingdom also ceased. And therefore we Christians, who have begun to call God Father in prayer, also pray that the kingdom of God may come to us.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the second petition of the Lord's Prayer, 'your kingdom come,' after having discussed the hallowing of God's name.

title: Praying that God's will be done in us
english: We also add and say: your will be done in heaven and on earth—not so that God does what he wills, but so that we may be able to do what God wills. For who resists God to prevent him from doing what he wills? But because the devil resists us, so that our mind and action do not obey God in everything, we pray and ask that God's will be done in us. For it to be done in us, there is need of God's will, that is, of his help and protection, because no one is strong by his own powers but is safe by God's indulgence and mercy. Finally, the Lord also, showing the weakness of the man he was bearing, says: Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me (Matthew 26:39). And giving his disciples an example, so that they do not their own will but God's, he added: yet not what I want but what you want (Matthew 26:39). And in another place he says: I have not come down from heaven to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me (John 6:38). But if the Son obeyed to do the Father's will, how much more should a servant obey to do the Lord's will, just as John in his letter also urges and instructs us to do God's will, saying: Do not love the world or the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him, because everything that is in the world is the desire of the flesh and the desire of the eyes and the ambition of the age, which is not from the Father but from the desire of the world. And the world will pass away, and its desire; but whoever does God's will remains forever, just as God also remains forever (1 John 2:15-17). We who want to remain forever must do the will of God, who is eternal.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the third petition of the Lord's Prayer, 'your will be done on earth as in heaven,' and why Christians must ask God to make them able to do his will.

title: The will of God is Christ's humility, faith, love, and endurance
english: But the will of God is what Christ both did and taught: humility in conduct, steadfastness in faith, restraint in words, justice in deeds, mercy in works, discipline in habits, not knowing how to do injury and being able to endure injury done, keeping peace with brothers and sisters, loving the Lord with the whole heart, loving in him that he is Father, fearing that he is God, preferring nothing at all to Christ, because he also preferred nothing to us, clinging inseparably to his love, standing by his cross bravely and confidently when there is a contest over his name and honor, showing in speech the constancy with which we confess, in trial the confidence with which we engage, in death the patience with which we are crowned. This is to will to be coheir of Christ; this is to do God's command; this is to fulfill the Father's will.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining what doing God's will means, after citing John on not loving the world.

title: The conflict of flesh and spirit and the prayer for God's will in both
english: We ask that God's will be done in heaven and on earth, and both of these concern the completion of our safety and salvation. For since we possess a body from the earth and a spirit from heaven, we ourselves are earth and heaven, and we pray that God's will be done in both—that is, in body and in spirit. There is a struggle between flesh and spirit, a daily conflict between them as they oppose each other, so that we do not do the very things we want: the spirit seeks heavenly and divine things, while the flesh desires earthly and worldly things. And so we ask that by God's help and aid concord be made between these two, so that while God's will is carried out in both spirit and flesh, the soul that has been reborn through him may be preserved. The apostle Paul declares this openly and clearly in his own voice: "The flesh desires against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh; for these are opposed to each other, so that you do not do the very things you want" (Galatians 5:17). "Now the works of the flesh are evident: adultery, fornication, impurity, filthiness, idolatry, sorcery, murders, enmities, contentions, rivalries, outbursts of anger, provocations, quarrels, dissensions, heresies, envy, drunkenness, carousing, and things like these. Those who do such things will not possess the kingdom of God" (Galatians 5:19-21). "But the fruit of the spirit is love, joy, peace, magnanimity, goodness, faith, gentleness, self-control, chastity" (Galatians 5:22-23). And therefore by daily, indeed by continuous prayers, we ask this: that God's will be done in heaven and on earth concerning us. For this is God's will: that earthly things yield to heavenly things, and spiritual and divine things prevail.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition 'your will be done on earth as in heaven' by applying it to the believer's own body and spirit.

title: Praying for the still-earthly
english: There is also another way to understand this, most beloved brothers. Since the Lord commands and warns us to love even our enemies and to pray for those who persecute us (Matthew 5:44), we should also pray for those who are still earth and have not yet begun to be heavenly. We ask that God's will be done in them as well—the will that Christ accomplished by preserving and restoring the human being. For when the disciples are no longer called earth by him but salt of the earth (Matthew 5:13), and the apostle calls the first man from the mud of the earth and the second from heaven (1 Corinthians 15:47), then rightly we too—who ought to be like God the Father, who makes his sun rise on the good and the evil and sends rain on the just and the unjust (Matthew 5:45)—pray and ask at Christ's instruction that we may make prayer for the salvation of all. Just as God's will has been done in heaven, that is, in us through our faith, so that we are from heaven, so may God's will also be done on earth, that is, in those unwilling to believe. so that those who are still earthly by their first birth may begin to be heavenly, born from water and the Spirit (John 3:5).
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition 'your will be done on earth as in heaven' by applying it to those not yet reborn from water and the Spirit.

title: Daily bread as Christ and the Eucharist
english: As the prayer continues, we ask and say: give us this day our daily bread. This can be understood both spiritually and simply, because each understanding serves our salvation by divine benefit. For Christ is the bread of life, and this bread is not everyone's, but ours. And just as we say our Father, because he is the Father of those who understand and believe, so we also call it our bread, because Christ is the bread of those of us who touch his body. We ask for this bread to be given to us daily, so that we who are in Christ and receive his Eucharist daily as the food of salvation may not, when some graver offense comes between, while abstaining and not communicating, be barred from the heavenly bread, and so be separated from Christ's body. He himself proclaims and says: I am the bread of life who came down from heaven. If anyone eats of my bread, he will live forever. And the bread that I will give is my flesh for the life of the world (John 6:51). Therefore, when he says that whoever eats of his bread will live forever, it is clear that those who touch his body and receive the Eucharist by the right of communion live. So on the other hand we must fear and pray that no one, while abstaining, is separated from Christ's body, remains far from salvation, with him himself threatening and saying: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you will not have life in you (John 6:53). And so we ask for our bread, that is, Christ, to be given to us daily, so that we who remain and live in Christ may not withdraw from his sanctification and body.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition 'give us this day our daily bread' in the Lord's Prayer, first in its spiritual sense as Christ received in the Eucharist.

title: Daily bread as contentment, not long-term desire
english: But it can also be understood this way: we who have renounced the world and cast away its riches and pomps through the faith of spiritual grace should ask for ourselves only food and sustenance. The Lord instructs this when he says, "Whoever does not renounce all that he has cannot be my disciple" (Luke 14:33). And whoever has begun to be Christ's disciple, renouncing everything according to his teacher's voice, ought to ask for daily food and not stretch out the desires of his petition into the long term. The Lord himself again prescribes this, saying, "Do not think about tomorrow, for tomorrow will think about itself. Sufficient for the day is its own evil" (Matthew 6:34). Rightly, then, does Christ's disciple ask for sustenance for the day, since he is forbidden to think about tomorrow. It would be contradictory and self-defeating for us to seek to live long in the world when we pray for the kingdom of God to come quickly. So also the blessed apostle warns, forming and strengthening the firmness of our hope and faith: "We brought nothing into this world, and we cannot take anything out. Having sustenance and covering, with these we are content. But those who want to become rich fall into temptation and snares and many harmful desires, which plunge a person into destruction and ruin. For the root of all evils is greed, and some, reaching for it, have made shipwreck of the faith and entangled themselves in many sorrows" (1 Timothy 6:7-10).
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition for daily bread, now arguing that it teaches Christians to ask only for each day's food and not to plan far ahead.

title: Riches are dangerous; the free man follows Christ
english: He teaches that riches are not only to be despised but are also dangerous, that in them is the root of flattering evils, the blindness of the human mind, deceived by hidden deception. So God rebukes the foolish rich man who was thinking about his worldly resources and boasting of the abundance of his overflowing harvests: "Fool, this night your soul is demanded. What you have prepared, whose will it be?" (Luke 12:20). The fool was rejoicing in his harvests on the night he was about to die, and the man whose life was already slipping away was thinking about the abundance of his food. But the Lord teaches that the one who sells everything, distributes it for the use of the poor, and stores up treasure for himself in heaven becomes perfect and complete. He says that the one who is unencumbered and girded, entangled in no snares of household property, but free and unbound, with his resources sent ahead to the Lord, himself following after them, can follow him and imitate the glory of the Lord's passion. So that each of us may be able to prepare himself for this, he learns to pray in this way and to know from the law of prayer what he ought to be.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition for daily bread, and has just cited Paul on contentment; he now contrasts the rich fool with the one who sells all and follows Christ.

title: God feeds the just and the wicked starve them
english: Daily bread cannot be lacking to the just man, since it is written: the Lord will not kill the soul of the just man by hunger (Proverbs 10:3), and again: I was young and I have grown old, and I have not seen the just man forsaken, nor his seed seeking bread (Psalm 37:25 (Psalm 36:25 in the Septuagint)). Likewise the Lord promises and says: Do not be anxious, saying, What shall we eat, or what shall we drink, or what shall we wear? For the nations seek all these things. But your Father knows that you need all these things. Seek first the kingdom and the justice of God, and all these things will be added to you (Matthew 6:31-33). To those who seek the kingdom and the justice of God, he promises that all things will be added. For since all things belong to God, nothing will be lacking to the one who has God, if he himself does not fail God. So Daniel, shut in the lions' den by the king's command, is provided a meal from heaven, and among hungry beasts that spare him the man of God is fed. So Elijah is nourished in flight and solitude, with ravens serving him and birds bringing him food in persecution. And—O detestable cruelty of human malice!—wild beasts spare, birds feed, and men plot against and rage!
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition for daily bread, arguing that God supplies all things to those who seek his kingdom and justice.

title: Forgiveness of debts as daily confession
english: After this we pray also for our sins, saying: and forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors (Matthew 6:12). After the provision of food, pardon of sin is asked for, so that the one who is fed by God may live in God, and provision may be made not only for this present and temporary life but for eternal life. We can come to that life if our sins are forgiven—the sins the Lord calls debts, as he says in his Gospel: I forgave you all that debt because you asked me (Matthew 18:32). How necessary, how provident and salutary, is the reminder that we are sinners, since we are compelled to pray for our sins! While pardon is being sought from God, the mind recalls its own conscience. So that no one may please himself as if he were innocent and perish by exalting himself, he is instructed and taught that he sins daily, since he is commanded daily to pray for his sins. This is what John also urges in his letter when he says: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us. But if we confess our sins, the Lord is faithful and just to forgive us our sins (1 John 1:8-9). In his letter he joined both things together: that we ought to pray for our sins, and that we obtain pardon when we pray. Therefore he called the Lord faithful, because he keeps faith with his promise to forgive sins; for the one who taught us to pray for our debts and sins promised fatherly mercy and the pardon that would follow.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition 'forgive us our debts' from the Lord's Prayer, after treating the petition for daily bread.

title: Forgive to be forgiven
english: He went on to add a law that binds us under a fixed condition and promise: we are to ask that our debts be forgiven us just as we ourselves forgive our debtors, knowing that what we ask for our sins cannot be obtained unless we do the same toward those who sin against us. That is why he also says in another place: With the measure you use, it will be measured back to you (Matthew 7:2). And the servant who, after his master forgave him his whole debt, refused to forgive his fellow servant is bound in prison (Matthew 18:28-34). Because he would not pardon his fellow servant, he lost what the Lord had pardoned to him. Christ sets this out still more forcefully in his commands, with the greater force of his severity. When you stand to pray, he says, forgive whatever you have against anyone, so that your Father in heaven may forgive you your sins. But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive you your sins (Mark 11:25; Matthew 6:15). You have no excuse left on the day of judgment, since you will be judged by your own sentence, and what you have done you will suffer yourself. For God has commanded those in his house to be peaceable, harmonious, and unanimous, and as he made us in the second birth, so he wills us to continue as reborn: we who are children of God are to remain in God's peace, and those who have one Spirit are to have one mind and one thought. So God does not receive the sacrifice of a person at odds with others, and he commands the one returning from the altar first to be reconciled to his brother, so that God may be at peace with peaceable prayers (Matthew 5:24). Our peace and brotherly concord and a people gathered into the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit are a greater sacrifice to God.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition about debts, and now presses the condition attached to it: we must forgive others if we want our own sins forgiven.

title: The sacrifice of the discordant cannot be cleansed even by martyrdom
english: For in the sacrifices that Abel and Cain first offered, God was not looking at their gifts but at their hearts, so that the one who was pleasing in heart was pleasing in his gift. Abel, peaceful and just, while sacrificing to God innocently, taught the rest of us that when we bring an offering to the altar, we should come with the fear of God, with a simple heart, with the law of justice, with the peace of concord. Rightly, since he was such a man in his sacrifice to God, he himself afterward became a sacrifice to God, so that by being the first to show martyrdom he inaugurated the Lord's passion with the glory of his own blood—he who had both the justice and the peace of the Lord. Such people are crowned by the Lord, and such people will be vindicated with the Lord on the day of judgment. But the one who is quarrelsome and divisive and does not have peace with his brothers, as the blessed apostle and holy Scripture testify, will not be able to escape the crime of fraternal dissension even if he will have been killed for the name, because as it is written, whoever hates his brother is a murderer (1 John 3:15), and a murderer does not reach the kingdom of heaven or live with God. The one who preferred to be an imitator of Judas rather than of Christ cannot be with Christ. What a sin it is that cannot be washed away even by the baptism of blood! What a crime it is that cannot be expiated even by martyrdom!
orientation: Cyprian is explaining why peace and concord are the true sacrifice God accepts, using Abel and Cain as the first examples.

title: God's permission is required before the adversary can act
english: Here too the Lord gives us a necessary command for our prayer: “And do not allow us to be led into temptation.” In this petition he shows that the adversary can do nothing against us unless God has first permitted it, so that all our fear, devotion, and watchfulness may be turned toward God, since in temptations evil is allowed no power unless power from there is granted. Scripture proves this when it says: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and was fighting against it, and the Lord gave it into his hand (2 Kings 25:1; cf. Jeremiah 52:4). But power against us is granted to evil according to our sins, as it is written: Who gave Jacob to plundering and Israel to those who were plundering him? Was it not God, against whom they sinned and were unwilling to walk in his ways or hear his law, and he brought upon them the fury of his soul (Isaiah 42:24)? And again, when Solomon sinned and departed from the Lord’s commands and ways, it is written: And the Lord stirred up Satan against Solomon himself (1 Kings 11:14).
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition 'and do not allow us to be led into temptation' from the Lord's Prayer, showing that the devil has no power over us unless God permits it.

title: Power given for punishment or for glory
english: Power is given against us in two ways: either for punishment when we sin, or for glory when we are tested. We see this in what happened to Job, with God declaring and saying: Look, I give into your hands everything he has; only beware not to touch him (Job 1:12). And the Lord says in the Gospel at the time of his passion: You would have no power against me unless it had been given to you from above (John 19:11). When we ask not to come into temptation, we are reminded of our weakness and feebleness by the very prayer we make, so that no one may insolently exalt himself, no one may arrogantly and proudly claim anything for himself, no one may consider the glory of confession or of suffering to be his own. For the Lord himself, teaching humility, said: Watch and pray, so that you do not come into temptation; the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak (Matthew 26:41). In this way, when a humble and lowly confession goes before, and everything asked in supplication with fear and honor of God is given wholly to God, it may be granted by his own mercy.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition 'lead us not into temptation' by showing that power over us is given by God either to punish sin or to prove the righteous, and that the petition teaches humility.

title: The final petition as complete protection
english: After all these things, at the end of the prayer comes a closing clause that gathers all our petitions and requests together in a brief conclusion. For at the very last we say: but deliver us from evil, taking in all the hostile things that the enemy contrives against us in this world. From which there can be firm and faithful protection if God delivers us, if he grants his help to us as we pray and implore him. When we say deliver us from evil, nothing remains that should still be asked for beyond this, once we ask for God's protection against evil. When that protection is obtained, we stand secure and safe against everything the devil and the world are working. For what fear of the world is there for someone whose guardian in the world is God?
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the last petition of the Lord's Prayer, 'but deliver us from evil,' after having treated the earlier petitions.

title: God's teaching shortens prayer and the law
english: What wonder is it, dearly beloved brothers, if the prayer is such as God taught, who by his own instruction shortened all our petition in a saving word? This had already been foretold through the prophet Isaiah, when he spoke full of the Holy Spirit about the majesty and goodness of God. “A word completing and shortening in righteousness,” he says, “for God will make a shortened word in the whole circle of the earth” (Isaiah 10:22-23; cf. Romans 9:28). For when the Word of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, came to all, and gathering the learned and the unlearned together, of every sex and age, he set forth the teachings of salvation, he made a great compendium of his commandments, so that in heavenly discipline the memory of those learning should not labor, but should quickly learn what was necessary for simple faith. Thus when he taught what eternal life is, he embraced the sacrament of life with great and divine brevity, saying: “This is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent” (John 17:3). Likewise, when he was selecting the first and greater commandments from the law and the prophets, he said: “Hear, Israel: the Lord your God is one Lord. And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength. This is the first, and the second is like it: you shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments the whole law and the prophets hang” (Mark 12:29-31). And again: “Whatever good things you wish people to do to you, do also to them. For this is the law and the prophets” (Matthew 7:12).
orientation: Cyprian is explaining why the Lord's Prayer is so brief: God himself taught it, and Scripture had foretold that God would make a shortened word on the earth.

title: Prayer by example, not only by words
english: God taught us to pray not only with words but also with deeds, praying and pleading often himself, and showing us by the testimony of his example what we ought to do. As it is written: “He himself was withdrawing into lonely places and praying” (Luke 5:16), and again: “He went out to the mountain to pray, and he was spending the night in prayer to God” (Luke 6:12). If he who was without sin prayed, how much more ought sinners to pray! And if he kept watch through the whole night, continually praying with unbroken prayers, how much more ought we to keep watch at night in frequenting prayer!
orientation: Cyprian is showing that the Lord taught prayer not only by his words but by his own practice of praying, and he now applies that example to sinners.

title: Christ's prayer for unity
english: But the Lord was praying and asking not for himself—what would an innocent man ask for himself?—but for our sins, as he himself makes clear when he says to Peter: “Behold, Satan demanded to have you, to vex you like wheat. But I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail” (Luke 22:31-32). And afterward he prays to the Father for all, saying: “I am not praying for these alone, but also for those who are going to believe in me through their word, that all may be one, just as you, Father, are in me and I in you, that they also may be in us” (John 17:20-21). Great is God’s kindness and likewise his love for our salvation, that he was not content to redeem us with his blood, but still prayed for us as well. See what the desire of the one praying was: that just as the Father and the Son are one, so we also may remain in that same unity. From this it can be understood how greatly the one sins who splits unity and peace, since the Lord prayed for this very thing, wanting his people to live, knowing that discord does not come to the kingdom of God.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining that the Lord prayed not for himself but for our sins and for the unity of all believers.

title: Watchfulness in prayer
english: But when we stand to pray, most beloved brothers, we must be watchful and press our whole heart into our prayers. Every carnal and worldly thought must leave, and the mind must think of nothing except the very thing it is praying for. That is why the priest, before the prayer, prepares the minds of the brothers with a preface, saying: “Lift up your hearts,” so that when the people answer, “We have them to the Lord,” they are reminded that they ought to think of nothing but the Lord. Let the breast be shut against the adversary and open to God alone, and let it not allow the enemy of God to approach it during the time of prayer. For he often creeps in and penetrates, and by subtle deceit calls our prayers away from God, so that we have one thing in the heart and another on the lips, when it is not the sound of the voice but the mind and understanding that ought to pray to the Lord with sincere intention. What sloth it is to be carried off and seized by foolish and profane thoughts when you are entreating the Lord, as if there were something else you ought to think about more than the fact that you are speaking with God. How do you ask God to hear you when you do not hear yourself? Do you want the Lord to remember you when you ask, when you yourself are not mindful of yourself? This is failing to guard against the enemy at all; this is offending the majesty of God by careless prayer when you pray to God; this is being awake with the eyes and asleep in the heart, when a Christian ought to be awake in heart even while sleeping with the eyes, as it is written from the person of the church speaking in the Song of Songs: “I sleep, but my heart is awake” (Song of Songs 5:2). Therefore the apostle carefully and cautiously warns, saying: “Be constant in prayer, watching in it” (Colossians 4:2), teaching and showing that those whom God sees watching in prayer are able to obtain from God what they ask.
orientation: Cyprian is addressing his fellow Christians about the inner disposition required when they stand to pray.

title: Prayer must be fruitful and joined with good works
english: Those who pray should not come to God with unfruitful and bare prayers. A petition is ineffective when a barren prayer is offered to God. For since every tree that does not produce fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire, so too a word that has no fruit cannot merit God, because it is fruitful through no work. And therefore the divine Scripture instructs, saying: “Prayer is good with fasting and almsgiving” (Tobit 12:8). For he who on the day of judgment will give reward for works and almsgiving is today also a kind hearer to the one who comes to prayer with work. Thus finally the centurion Cornelius, when he prayed, deserved to be heard. He was one who did many almsgivings among the people and always prayed to God. To him, praying about the ninth hour, an angel stood by, giving testimony of his work and saying: “Cornelius, your prayers and your almsgivings have ascended as a memorial before God” (Acts 10:3-4).
orientation: Cyprian is urging that prayer must not be empty but accompanied by good works, and he introduces Cornelius as an example of prayer joined with almsgiving.

title: Works lift prayer to God
english: Prayers ascend quickly to God when the merits of our work place them before God. So also the angel Raphael stood by Tobit, who was always praying and always working, and said: “It is honorable to reveal and confess the works of God. For when you and Sarah were praying, I offered the remembrance of your prayer in the sight of the glory of God. And when you buried the dead simply, and because you did not hesitate to rise and leave your dinner, but went and buried the dead man, and I was sent to test you. And again God sent me to heal you and Sarah your daughter-in-law. For I am Raphael, one of the seven righteous angels who stand and dwell before the glory of God” (Tobit 12:12-15). Through Isaiah also the Lord admonishes and teaches, bearing witness to similar things: “Loose,” he says, “every knot of injustice, loose the bonds of contracts that strangle the powerless. Let the broken go free into rest, and scatter every unjust contract. Break your bread to the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house. If you see the naked, clothe them, and do not despise your own kin. Then your early light will break forth, and your garments will quickly shine forth, and righteousness will go before you, and the glory of God will surround you. Then you will cry out, and God will hear you. While you are still speaking, he says: Here I am” (Isaiah 58:6-9). He promises that he is present, and says that he hears and protects those who loosen the knots of injustice from their hearts and do almsgiving among God's household according to his commands. While they hear what God commands to be done, they themselves also deserve to be heard by God. The blessed apostle Paul, helped by the brothers in a time of pressing need, said that the works that are done are sacrifices to God. “I am filled,” he says, “receiving from Epaphroditus the things sent by you, odors of sweetness, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God” (Philippians 4:18). For when someone has mercy on the poor, he lends to God, and when he gives to the least, he gives to God, spiritually sacrificing to God odors of sweetness.
orientation: Cyprian is continuing his argument that prayer must be joined with good works, now giving examples from Raphael, Isaiah, and Paul.

title: The hours of prayer and the Trinity
english: But in celebrating prayers, we find that Daniel and the three boys, strong in faith and victors in captivity, observed the third hour, the sixth, and the ninth—namely by the sacrament of the Trinity, which had to be manifested in the last times. For the first hour coming to the third shows the completed number of the Trinity, and likewise the fourth proceeding to the sixth declares a second Trinity, and when the ninth is completed from the seventh, a perfect Trinity is numbered through each three hours. Those who worshipped God, determining these spaces of hours spiritually long ago, served at fixed and lawful times for prayer. And afterward the matter was made clear: these were sacraments of old, because the righteous prayed in this way before. For at the third hour the Holy Spirit descended upon the disciples, fulfilling the grace of the Lord's promise. Likewise Peter, going up to the housetop at the sixth hour, was instructed by a sign and also by the voice of God warning him to admit all to the grace of salvation, since he had previously doubted about cleansing the Gentiles. And the Lord, crucified at the sixth hour to the ninth, washed away our sins with His blood, and so that He might redeem and vivify us, He then completed the victory by His passion.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining that the fixed hours of prayer observed by the righteous of old were signs of the Trinity, later fulfilled in the events of Christ and the Spirit.

title: Christ the true sun and day makes every hour a time for prayer
english: But for us, dearly beloved brothers, beyond the hours observed of old, both the times and the sacred rites of prayer have now increased. For we must also pray in the morning, so that the Lord's resurrection may be celebrated by morning prayer. The Holy Spirit indicated this long ago in the Psalms, saying: "My king and my God, because to you I will pray, Lord, in the morning; and you will hear my voice. In the morning I will stand before you and see you" (Psalm 5:2-3; 5:3-4 in the Septuagint). And again the Lord speaks through the prophet: "At dawn they will keep watch for me, saying: Let us go and return to the Lord our God" (Hosea 6:1). Likewise, when the sun withdraws and the day ceases, we must necessarily pray again. For since Christ is the true sun and the true day, when the sun and the day of this world withdraw, we pray and ask that light may come upon us again; we pray for the coming of Christ, who will provide the grace of eternal light. The Holy Spirit declares in the Psalms that Christ is called the day: "The stone," he says, "which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner. This was done by the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes. This is the day which the Lord has made; let us rejoice and feast in it" (Psalm 118:22-24). Likewise, the prophet Malachi testifies that he is called the sun, saying: "But for you who fear the name of the Lord, the sun of righteousness will rise, and healing is in his wings" (Malachi 4:2). But if in the holy Scriptures Christ is the true sun and the true day, no hour is excepted for Christians, but God must be adored frequently and always, so that we who are in Christ—that is, in the sun and in the true day—may persist through the whole day in prayers and may pray. And when night, rolled back, succeeds by the law of the world running its alternating course, no harm can come to those who pray from the darkness of night, because for children of light it is day even in the night. For when is he without light who has light in his heart? Or when does he not have sun and day for whom Christ is sun and day?
orientation: Cyprian is addressing his fellow Christians, explaining that now, beyond the old fixed hours of prayer, every time—morning, evening, and night—has become a time for prayer because Christ is the true sun and day.

title: Night as day for those in Christ
english: But we who are in Christ—that is, in the light—are always in the light, and we must not cease from prayer even in the nights. So Anna the widow, praying without interruption, always watchful, persisted in deserving well of God, as it is written in the Gospel: "She did not withdraw from the temple, serving with fastings and prayers night and day" (Luke 2:37). Let the gentiles see to it—those not yet enlightened—or the Jews, who have been forsaken by the light and have remained in darkness. But we, dearly beloved brothers, who are always in the light of the Lord, who remember and hold what we have begun to be through the grace we have received, let us count night as day. Let us believe that we are always walking in the light; let us not be hindered by the darkness we have escaped. Let there be no losses of prayers in the night hours, no lazy and slothful wastings of prayer. Recreated spiritually and reborn through the indulgence of God, let us imitate what we shall be: we who will possess in the kingdom only day, without the interruption of night, let us keep watch in the night as in the light. We who will always pray and give thanks to God, let us not cease to pray and give thanks here as well.
orientation: Cyprian is closing the treatise by urging Christians, who live in Christ the true light, to keep praying even at night.
